subject: Zenith enterprise RFP: throughput envelope & surge-evidence pack
messages:
From: Sam Price <sam.price@zenithai.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Cc: procure@zenithai.com
Date: 2025-08-18T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: RFP - performance artifacts request (throughput + tail latency)

Hi Grace,

Thanks for taking our RFP. To move the performance section forward we need the following artifacts by EOD Aug 22: a) a concise throughput envelope (QPS vs model/instance type) for the recommended model variants, b) tail latency quantiles (p50/p95/p99/p99.9) for typical short and long sequences, c) documented surge/burst behavior and graceful degradation modes, and d) any runbook or reproduction steps you can share so our SREs can replay the tests.

We're particularly sensitive to p99.9 for chat workloads and want concrete evidence of behaviour under load spikes (10x baseline for short windows). If you can provide CSV/plots and a short runbook, that will help our procurement and infra teams finalize the technical evaluation.

Please confirm what you can deliver and when. If you prefer, we can schedule a 30m call with SREs to walk through the results.

Thanks,
Sam Price
Head of Platform Engineering
ZenithAI

[Attachment: zenith_rfp_performance_qs.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet)]

From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
To: Sam Price <sam.price@zenithai.com>
Cc: Beth Tran <beth.tran@zenithai.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-08-18T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: RE: RFP - performance artifacts request (throughput + tail latency)

Sam — thanks for the clear ask and the spreadsheet. We can deliver an evidence pack that covers all four items you listed by Aug 22. Attached you'll find a first-pass dataset with the throughput envelope CSV and a short executive summary; we'll follow up with burst plots and a short runbook by EOD on Aug 21 so you have time to review.

Quick notes on scope:
- Models: we'll include two recommended variants (medium and high-capacity) using the open weights you referenced in the RFP.
- Workloads: short chat tokens (avg 60 tokens) and long context batch (avg 1,200 tokens) — we'll provide separate quantile tables.
- Surge scenarios: 1x baseline, 4x sustained ramp, and 10x short-window spike (30s) with fallback behavior documented.

Attachments in this message: redwood_throughput_envelope.csv, executive_summary.txt. The full burst_evidence_plots.pdf and a reproduction runbook (repro_runbook.md) will follow tomorrow.

If you want a call, suggest Aug 22 10:00 AM PT — happy to loop in our performance lead Ben for the tech walk-through.

Best,
Grace O'Connor
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
Grace.OConnor@redwood.com

[Attachment: redwood_throughput_envelope.csv (text/csv)]
[Attachment: executive_summary.txt (text/plain)]

From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-08-19T09:36:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: RFP - performance artifacts request (throughput + tail latency) — internal alignment

Team — forwarding Zenith's initial ask and our reply. Action items:
1) Ben: own the tech walk-through on Aug 22 (10:00 AM PT tentative). Prepare a 15-min demo of the surge test and fallback logs (showing model variant fallback and cache hit impacts).
2) Marissa: coordinate a concise SOW bullet for the procurement packet — include testing scope and what we will not provide (e.g., third-party load injector licensing).
3) Karthik: confirm the runbook steps and check the reproducibility notes for the 10x short-window spike; ensure we include the exact kernel selection and quantization settings used.

Notes on benchmarking methodology to include in the runbook (short bullets we should capture in the deliverable):
- Load generation: multi-source qps fan with interleaved chat/long-context workloads; seed traffic to match tenant prefix distributions.
- Metrics: token QPS, request QPS, end-to-end latency, model time (compute-only), p50/p95/p99/p99.9 for both API and compute lanes.
- Cache behavior: measure cold vs warm prefix K/V cache and include delta breakdowns.
- Graceful degradation: document fallback to model variant X-quantized with throughput/latency tradeoffs and expected quality delta (example prompts + outputs).

I've attached the draft runbook and the initial CSV so you can validate. Ben — can you confirm you'll capture logs showing automatic fallback events? Karthik — please add the kernel/compilation notes inline.

Thanks,
Grace

[Attachment: repro_runbook.md (text/markdown)]
[Attachment: redwood_throughput_envelope.csv (text/csv)]

From: Beth Tran <beth.tran@zenithai.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>, Sam Price <sam.price@zenithai.com>
Cc: procure@zenithai.com
Date: 2025-08-20T16:45:00-07:00
Subject: RE: RFP - performance artifacts request (throughput + tail latency)

Grace — appreciate the quick turnaround. We reviewed the CSV and the draft runbook; high level this looks good. A couple of clarifications before we proceed to procurement:

1) For the 10x short-window scenario, can you include the exact number of concurrent injectors and the inter-arrival distribution used? We want to replicate the same test in our lab.
2) On graceful degradation: please add a table that maps traffic level -> fallback chain -> expected p99 change and any quality delta notes.
3) Can you confirm whether the throughput envelope CSV uses cold-start inclusive or excludes cold starts? It wasn't explicit.

We will tentatively accept Aug 22 10:00 AM PT for the technical walk-through. Please attach the final burst_evidence_plots.pdf and the annotated runbook in the same Drive link you provided so I can share with the SREs.

If all good, procurement will prepare the draft contract and we can align on SLO language for the dedicated capacity option.

Regards,
Beth Tran
Director, Infrastructure Engineering
ZenithAI
